title: Did a coronavirus cause the pandemic known as the “Russian flu”?
short: Doctors called the pandemic of 1889 influenza. Their case notes and death registers could help decide whether a coronavirus better explains whom it sickened and killed.
matters: One candidate is OC43, a coronavirus that circulates in people today. Estimates from modern viruses place its common ancestor with a cattle coronavirus near the late nineteenth century. If OC43 was responsible, a pandemic long used as an example of influenza would belong to a different disease history.
stuck: A date for a common ancestor gives a range of years and cannot identify the virus in a particular patient. Doctors also differed in what they asked about. A report of lost smell or prolonged exhaustion is hard to interpret without knowing how often the same doctor recorded it in other epidemics.
solved: Compare symptom frequencies and age-specific excess deaths with the 1847–48 and 1918 influenza outbreaks in comparable places and records. Report which explanation each pattern favours and by how much. A definitive viral identification would require direct evidence from the pandemic itself.
approach: Start with Henry Franklin Parsons’s survey, local medical reports and municipal death returns. Keep physician accounts separate from newspaper reprints.
Record the number of patients actually described, their ages and whether each symptom was mentioned, denied or left unexamined.
Compare like reporting settings across outbreaks. Test whether conclusions survive removing a city, a wave or an unusually detailed observer.

needs.ask: Compare the symptom and age patterns across outbreaks with allowance for differences in who was examined.
Estimate deaths above the usual seasonal level in cities with age-specific population counts.
